title: Enforcement — design
subtitle: Idea · model · invariants · functions · mockups · dashboard · path

sections.title: A block is a written decision, not a flag
sections.body:
> At any moment we can answer: why can't this team send, who decided that, and what would change it?

Today the reason almost always exists for a moment and is never written next to the block:

- `handleDisableNewDomain` receives `disableCriterion` and only logs it.
- The New Signups bulk action wrote its decision to `AdminPanelInteraction`, not to the domain.
- The health cron writes a notice row, then flips `disabled` with no link back.

**The design:** every reason something can't send or publish is a row, written once at the moment of the decision, saying what was found, who decided, and on what evidence. "Disabled" is just whether any of those rows are still in effect.

sections.title: Today: 2,746 disabled domains, none with a reason
sections.body:
Production, Oct 31. The latest `DisableDomainEvent` for each disabled domain:

| Latest event | Domains | Means |
|---|---|---|
| none | 1,966 | no record on the domain (mostly the old New Signups bulk action, to confirm) |
| Pending | 436 | someone acted, nobody decided — the real backlog |
| BlockDomain | 330 | a person upheld it, reason unknown |
| Reenable / Unleash | 14 | record says enabled, domain is disabled |

Deletion-requested teams are only 74 of these.

The same idea also lives in four other fields, each with its own switch and no decider:

| Field | Is really |
|---|---|
| `SendingDomain.disabled` | a block on a domain |
| `EmailMessage.safetyClassification = "phishing"` | a block on one email |
| `safetyClassification = <override>` | an exception for that email, no who/why/expiry |
| `Team.skipSafetyChecks` | a permanent team-wide exception, no who/why/expiry |
| `CampaignContent.isSafeContent` | a detector's verdict — evidence, not a decision |

sections.title: Three tables and a list in code
sections.body:
```
Restriction                         one reason something is blocked
  teamId
  scope       team | sendingDomain | email      + sendingDomainId? / emailMessageId?
  effect      send | publish
  category    "content.phishing", "list.purchased", "signup.review_blocked"…  (registry)
  ruleId?     which detector rule; empty for a person
  findingKey? "email:clx…" · "word:bitcoin" · "notice:clx…"
  decidedBy   "automation@health-v3" | userId
  note?       required when a person decided                       CHECK
  createdAt
  upheldBy?, upheldAt?                a person looked and agreed
  liftedBy?, liftedAt?, verdict?, liftNote?    all or none          CHECK
     verdict: wrong | fixed  (+ reclassified, legacy rows only)

RestrictionEvidence                 what inspired it
  restrictionId, kind (notice | email | suspiciousActivity | adminInteraction | url), ref

Allowance                           "don't flag this again", until a date
  teamId, selector (finding | rule | category), grantedBy, until, note, revokedAt?
```

**Registry** (code, not schema): each category's default scope and effect, and the words a sender sees. Adding a reason is a code change with a test, never a migration.

**Fixed by the database:** who it applies to, what it stops, who decided, lifted all-or-nothing, a note when a person decided. **Grows without a migration:** categories, rules, finding kinds, evidence kinds. **Never:** a JSON details column, or a status column someone writes by hand.

sections.title: Scope × effect covers every block we have
sections.body:
**Send** = nothing goes out. **Publish** = no new or edited content goes live; what's already live keeps sending.

| You want to… | scope | effect |
|---|---|---|
| Stop all sending for a team (SES suspension, ban) | team | send |
| Disable one domain (today's case) | sendingDomain | send |
| Hold one flagged email, the rest keep sending | email | send |
| New account: nothing new goes live until reviewed | team | publish |
| Hold one publish for review (LOO-6309) | email | publish |

A team covers its domains and emails; a domain covers emails sent from it. No precedence: anything in the way blocks, and each reason is lifted on its own.

**Not restrictions:** `campaignSizeLimit`, `maxPreviewsPerDay`, rate limits, `trustLevel`. A restriction is a decision about a finding; a setting is how much of something a team gets.

sections.title: What must always be true
sections.body:
1. **Every restriction has a reason and a decider.** `category` ∧ (`ruleId` ∨ person) ∧ `decidedBy`.
   *Breaks when* something is blocked and nobody can say which check or person did it.
2. **The remedy matches the finding.** Lift and allow act on one restriction or one finding, never "the domain".
   *Breaks when* approving one email re-enables a domain blocked for a complaint spike — live today.
3. **Detectors are provisional, people are binding.** Only a person lifts, with a verdict and a note; allowances expire.
   *Breaks when* a re-enable leaves no record of whether the detector misfired.
4. **Write once, compute everything else.** Only `restrict()` and `lift()` change anything; status, timeline, banner and API are reads.
   *Breaks when* any code writes `disabled` directly, or edits a past row.
5. **Evidence explains, never decides.** State reads restrictions only; notices, emails and links are attached, not consulted.
   *Breaks when* "is it blocked" and "why" can disagree.

sections.title: check(): the one definition of blocked
restrict() and lift(): the only writers
sections.body:
```ts
/** Writes a restriction, then sets each covered domain's `disabled` from check(), in one transaction. */
restrict({ teamId, scope, effect, category, ruleId?, findingKey?, decidedBy, note?, evidence[] })

/** Records a person's verdict on one restriction, then recomputes; re-enables only if nothing else is in effect. */
lift({ restrictionId, liftedBy, verdict: "wrong" | "fixed", note, allow?: { until } })

uphold({ restrictionId, upheldBy })
```

`SendingDomain.disabled` stays as a **cached copy** for the send path. Only these functions write it, always from `check()` after the row lands. A nightly job compares the copy with the rows and alerts on any mismatch.

All of today's writes already go through three query functions in `queries/sending-domain.ts` (since #11090–#11131), so locking them behind `restrict`/`lift` is small.

sections.title: Reviewer · what keeps this blocked
sections.body:
```
admin › team › acme                                  mail.acme-example.com
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ ■ Can't send — 2 reasons. Lifting both re-enables.                   │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Possible phishing · "Reset your password"     waiting   [Uphold][Lift…]│
│ email · send · automation@scan-v14 · Oct 28 14:07                    │
│ Evidence: AI verdict · the email ↗                                   │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Complaint rate 0.41% over 24h                 waiting   [Uphold][Lift…]│
│ domain · send · automation@health-v3 · Oct 28 15:52                  │
│ Evidence: Spam notice at Error ↗ (chart)                             │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ ░ Banned word "bitcoin" · "Weekly digest"                    lifted  │
│ ░ Dana R. · wrong · "crypto newsletter" · allowed until Jan 27       │

Each row is one restriction. The header is `check()`; it can't disagree with the rows.

sections.title: Reviewer · lift, and how you know it's no longer blocking
sections.body:
**Lift** = "this reason no longer blocks". It's today's Re-enable, aimed at one reason. Nothing is deleted.

```
Lift: Possible phishing · "Reset your password"

  (●) The check was wrong          ( ) The sender fixed it
  [✓] Don't flag this email again until [ Jan 27 ]

  Note  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │ Their own app's reset email, links to them.  │
        └──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                                         [Cancel] [Lift]
```

After Lift, the panel answers "is it still blocked?" directly:

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ ■ Can't send — 1 reason left.                                        │
│ Complaint rate 0.41% over 24h        waiting   [Uphold][Lift…]       │
│ ░ Possible phishing · lifted just now · You · wrong                  │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
toast: "Lifted. mail.acme still can't send: complaint rate (Oct 28 15:52)."
```
Lift the last one and the header turns to **Sending**, and `disabled` flips in the same transaction.

sections.title: Admin · block by hand, with off-platform evidence
sections.body:
```
Block acme
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Applies to   ( ) Team   (●) mail.acme-example.com   ( ) One email…
Stops        (●) Sending   ( ) Publishing
Reason       [ Purchased or scraped list              ▾ ]
               the sender is told this one, in our words

Evidence     ☑ Spam complaints at Error · Oct 28 15:52
             ☐ Flagged email "Reset your password" · Oct 28
             + Link  https://support…/thread/8812

Note         ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
(internal)   │ Replied to support admitting a bought list.  │
             └──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                                         [Cancel]  [Block]
```
Reason and note required; evidence optional. Off-platform evidence is a link plus the note — customer messages stay in the support tool.

sections.title: Sender · banner and API
sections.body:
```
app › campaigns
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ ⚠ Sending from mail.acme-example.com is paused              │
│   One of your emails, "Reset your password", looked like    │
│   phishing to our automated checks. We're reviewing it and  │
│   will email you by the end of the next business day.       │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
```
POST /api/v1/transactional  → 403
{ "success": false,
  "message": "Sending from mail.acme-example.com is paused.",
  "reason": { "category": "content.phishing",
              "summary": "An email looked like phishing to our automated checks.",
              "next": "under_review" } }
```
Both read `check().blocking` and the registry's words. Notes never reach the sender.

sections.body:

Campaign "Black Friday" → [Publish]
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

│   we'll publish them once they're reviewed.  (LOO-6309)    │

```
Same table, scope `email`, effect `send` or `publish`. Same reviewer panel, same Lift.

sections.title: The guiding question, for the whole fleet
sections.body:
> Across every team: what's blocked, why, who decided, and are our decisions right?

The sender, support and reviewer views answer it for **one** team, and they come free from the kernel. The dashboard answers it for **all** of them, and it's the only place the last part — *are we right?* — can be seen.

**It is only reads.** Every number is a query over restrictions, evidence and allowances (rule 4). No counters, no nightly rollups that can drift; a slow query gets a cache keyed by the rows, never a second source of truth. `stateAt(rows, t)` makes every panel answerable at any past moment, so "last Tuesday" is a parameter, not a snapshot someone remembered to take.

sections.title: Detector scorecards: where 'are we right' lives
sections.body:
Each lift records a verdict, so each rule gets a measured record:

| Column | Query over restrictions with this `ruleId` |
|---|---|
| blocks | started in the window |
| upheld | a person agreed (`upheldAt`) |
| wrong | lifted with verdict `wrong` — the false-positive rate |
| fixed | lifted with verdict `fixed` — the detector was right, the sender changed |
| waiting | still in effect, nobody decided |
| to decide | median time from start to upheld/lifted |

**⚠** when `wrong / decided` passes a threshold, or jumps against the previous window. That's the signal to tune or retire a rule, and it's the evidence for the change.

Grouped by `decidedBy` version too (`scan-v13` vs `scan-v14`), so a detector change shows whether it got better.

sections.title: v0: what today's data can already show
sections.body:
Before any new table, the same page can run on what we store now, each panel labeled **inferred**:

| Panel | From today's tables |
|---|---|
| Blocked now | `SendingDomain.disabled`, split by latest `DisableDomainEvent.decision` (the 2,746 table) |
| Waiting | `DisableDomainEvent` Pending, oldest first (436 today) |
| Unexplained | disabled with no event, or no admin record (1,966 today) |
| Flagged emails waiting | `EmailMessage.safetyClassification = "phishing"`, not reviewed |
| Health trips | `AccountLimitNotice` at Error per day, fleet-wide (the chart, for every team) |
| Signup blocks | `AdminPanelInteraction` "New Signups bulk action" per day, per admin |

What v0 **can't** show: per-detector wrong rates (re-enables carry no verdict) and per-reason state. That gap, on the page in plain words, is the argument for the restriction tables.

v0 also sets the baseline: when v1 ships, the same tiles compare against what v0 measured.

sections.title: Alerts: three things that should page
sections.body:
1. **Unexplained went up.** After step 3 nothing is blocked without a reason; an increase means something wrote `disabled` around `restrict()`. The nightly check names the domain.
2. **The queue is older than the promise.** Oldest waiting block past the review time we tell senders ("end of the next business day").
3. **A detector's wrong rate jumped.** Against its previous window, on enough decisions to mean it.

The page shows the same three at the top when they're firing. Alerting itself goes through our existing observability, as Terraform, not a script.

sections.title: Where it lives
sections.body:
**A tab in the Loops admin** ("Enforcement"), next to Disabled Domains and the team page. It's for the people who review, it links straight into the reviewer panel and the team page, and it uses the same tRPC + query/model layering as everything else.

Branch shape, ladder order:
1. queries: one per panel, each a single read with its test
2. model: the scorecard math and the "dragging / ⚠" thresholds, fake deps
3. wiring: one admin route returning the page
4. UI: the tab — stat tiles, the queue, the scorecard table, small-multiple sparklines

v0 is that forest on today's tables; v1 swaps each query onto restrictions, panel by panel.

sections.title: Backfill: recover reasons we already wrote down
sections.body:
Every disabled domain needs a restriction on day one, or computing `disabled` would re-enable it.

| Domain today | Becomes |
|---|---|
| has an `AdminPanelInteraction` decision (e.g. New Signups bulk) | `signup.review_blocked`, decided by that admin, upheld then |
| latest event `BlockDomain`, no admin record | `legacy.unrecorded`, upheld (by unknown — allowed on legacy only) |
| latest event `Pending`, or nothing | `legacy.unrecorded`, waiting for review, nearby signals attached as evidence |
| latest event `Reenable`/`Unleash` (14) | same, **and** listed for a look before anything ships |

Reviewers clear legacy rows with **Reclassify** (write the real reason, lift the legacy row as `reclassified`) or **Lift**.

**The number:** legacy restrictions in effect on active teams. It starts near 2,700 and can only go down, because after step 2 nothing is blocked without a reason.

sections.title: Order of work
sections.body:
1. **Improve what we have** (no new tables) — notice chart ✓ built; replace the notice-card flood with a link to it.
2. **Tables + registry.** No behavior change.
3. **Every disable writes a restriction** with its real reason, alongside today's write. New blocks are explained from this deploy on.
4. **Backfill** current blocks (recover from admin records first), then turn on the nightly check.
5. **Lock writers**: only `restrict`/`lift` touch `disabled`.
6. **Reviewer panel, lift, uphold, allowances** — fixes approve-re-enables-everything for real.
7. **Sender banner + API reason.**
8. **Email scope and publish effect**: phishing classification, override constant, `skipSafetyChecks`, LOO-6309 — one old field at a time: write rows for current values, move readers to `check()`, stop writing the field.

sections.title: Still to decide
sections.body:
- **Review promise.** What review time do we tell senders? The queue alert keys off it.
- **Reviewer view.** Show decisions per reviewer on the dashboard, or keep that out to avoid it reading as surveillance?
- **The reason list.** What do admins actually block for? Support likely knows better than the code.
- **Evidence links.** Any URL, or only our support tool (so the panel can say "support thread")?
- **Upheld** as its own state — I'd keep it; it's today's BlockDomain and rule 3.
- **Publish for workflows.** Does a team-wide publish hold stop editing a live workflow's email, or only new ones?
- **`skipSafetyChecks`** as an allowance needs an expiry and a note. Which teams have it, and who set it?
- **Complaint-rate denominator** excludes only exact `@gmail.com`; fix it or label it.
